scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Tight but realistic slippage (e.g. 0.1–0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you…
MEV-protected / private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this)
Split large trades. Avoid thin pools
Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs
scenes.vo: M.E.V. (maximal extractable value) is profit taken by whoever orders transactions in a block. Some is harmless (arbitrage realigning prices). The kind that hurts you: (pushing the price up), lets your trade execute at the worse price, then sells just after. Your slippage tolerance is its profit ceiling. Defences: Sandwich attack: a bot sees your pending swap, buys just before you Tight but realistic slippage (for example 0.1–0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you understand why) M.E.V.-protected / private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this) Split large trades. Avoid thin pools Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs
scenes.cap: Sandwich attack: a bot sees your pending swap, buys just before you Tight but realistic slippage (e.g. 0.1–0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you understand why) MEV-protected / private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this) Split large trades. Avoid thin pools Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: 3%, up to about $600. 0.5%, up to about $100. Private / protected route, Transaction isn't visible in the public mempool, so it can't be sandwiched from there.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Slippage set for this pair and size, never left at a high default
Protected routing on for larger swaps
Large orders split or routed through deep liquidity
